classification.difficultyReason: Two scaffolded tangent calculations supply perpendicular ground lengths for Pythagoras.

content.prompt: Consider the diagram of a tent pole secured by two wires and pegs. Give distances to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Pole and two wires with perpendicular ground directions, base right-angle marks, peg names, Tent and Pole labels, and a horizontal height leader. Ordinary source blue strokes become black.
spec.mathematics: Vertical pole height 2.1 m; elevation angles 43 degrees at peg A and 39 degrees at peg B; ground distances from the pole base are perpendicular.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the distance from the base of the pole to peg $A$.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the distance from the pole base to peg $A$.
$$\begin{aligned}\tan43^\circ&=\frac{2.1}{x}\\x&=\frac{2.1}{\tan43^\circ}\\x&\approx2.25\text{ m}\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the distance from the base of the pole to peg $B$.

answer.worked:
Let $y$ be the distance from the pole base to peg $B$.
$$\begin{aligned}\tan39^\circ&=\frac{2.1}{y}\\y&=\frac{2.1}{\tan39^\circ}\\y&\approx2.59\text{ m}\end{aligned}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the distance between peg $A$ and peg $B$.

answer.worked:
The ground distances are perpendicular. Using their unrounded values,
$$\begin{aligned}AB^2&=x^2+y^2\\AB&=\sqrt{\left(\frac{2.1}{\tan43^\circ}\right)^2+\left(\frac{2.1}{\tan39^\circ}\right)^2}\\AB&\approx3.43\text{ m}\end{aligned}$$
